pairs.question: Rusticus es?
pairs.answer: nescis quid Graeco nomine dicar: spuma vocor nitri.
pairs.derivation: Quoted Martial couplet on aphronitrum, introduced by Isidore's framing 'De quo quidam ait', which is dropped as a speech tag. The speaker poses the question 'Rusticus es?' and answers it himself: if you are a rustic, you do not know the Greek name, so I am called (Latin) 'spuma nitri'. Window ends at the full stop after 'spuma vocor nitri'; what follows ('Graecus es? aphronitrum.') is the parallel second question/answer, taken as a separate pair.

pairs.question: Graecus es?
pairs.derivation: Second clause of the same Martial couplet: the speaker asks 'Graecus es?' and answers with the Greek name 'aphronitrum'. Starts after the full stop following 'spuma vocor nitri'; nothing follows in the couplet (the verse-line / footer scaffolding is excluded).
